channel.description: Get the latest technology news, AI developments, startup funding updates, business enterprise and IT industry insights, cybersecurity alerts, and digital policy trends from India and around the world on ET Tech

item.title: Trump administration plans to move AI testing agency officials to White House: The Information
item.description: The Trump administration is planning to move three senior officials of the Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence to the White House, The Information reported on Monday, citing a White House official.

item.title: UK given access to safety-test latest AI models, minister says
item.description: Scrutiny of AI safety has intensified after developers including Anthropic and OpenAI disclosed instances of rogue or undesired behaviour by AI agents. Some industry figures have warned the technology could pose an existential threat to humanity.

item.title: Dating app Bumble in advanced talks to go private at $1 billion valuation, source says
item.description: Shares of Bumble rose around 21% in afternoon trading. Reuters exclusively reported earlier this year that Bumble is exploring a sale amid slowing growth in the online dating ​sector.

item.title: Meta releases Muse Wonder AI models to challenge Anthropic and OpenAI
item.description: The launch comes after CEO Mark Zuckerberg pledged billions of dollars and aggressively poached researchers over the past year to catch up in Silicon Valley's intensifying AI race.

item.title: Qualcomm sells nearly 1% stake in Shadowfax Technologies for Rs 157 crore
item.description: Qualcomm Ventures, through its affiliate Qualcomm Asia Pacific Pte Ltd, sold a little over 57.13 lakh shares, representing a 0.98% stake, in Bengaluru-based Shadowfax Technologies, according to bulk deal data on the BSE.

item.title: Govt selects 19 fund managers under RDI, committing Rs 7,131 crore
item.description: The government's Research, Development and Innovation Fund (RDIF) has approved its first cohort of 19 second-level fund managers with a total commitment of Rs 7,131 crore, marking a key step towards mobilising private investment in research and development and emerging technologies.

item.title: Microsoft plans huge deployment of its own AI chips, with an eye on saving costs
item.description: The Maia 300, as the chip is called, is the third generation of the company's custom chips designed to handle AI data crunching such as coding and carrying out complex business tasks on a user's behalf. Its predecessor is already running Microsoft's in-house AI models, as well as models from OpenAI delivered on Microsoft's Azure cloud computing service.

item.title: The Wealth Company AIF invests Rs 400 crore in Boldfit
item.description: Founded in 2018 by Pallav Bihani, Boldfit offers sportswear, athletic footwear, sports equipment, and fitness essentials. It has grown at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of more than 80% over the past three years and serves over 2 crore customers annually, according to a company statement.

item.title: IonQ to buy cybersecurity firm Elisity in up to $1.3 billion deal
item.description: Quantum computing company IonQ said on Monday it would buy cybersecurity firm Elisity in an all-stock deal valued at up to $1.3 billion, as it looks to expand its quantum security business.

item.title: Norway fines Microsoft's Xandr $9.6 million over Grindr data sharing
item.description: Xandr relayed data revealing the sexual orientation of users of Grindr, a dating app for LGBTQIA+ people, to companies in automated ad auctions from July 2018 to April 2020.

item.title: Philippine lower house approves bill restricting minors' social media access
item.description: The Philippines is the latest country, from Greece and Portugal to Australia, Malaysia and Indonesia, to try to curb social media use by minors, as concern grows over its effects on child health and safety.

item.title: GE Aerospace to nearly double supplier spend in India by 2030, eyes growing aviation demand
item.description: The announcement was made alongside the release of a report by Ernst & Young (EY), titled 'Powering Progress: GE Aerospace's Economic Impact in India', which assesses the company's economic contribution to India's commercial aviation, defence, manufacturing and engineering sectors over four decades.

item.title: US reverses course on Britain's testing of AI models
item.description: American AI developers can give the British government early access to AI models for safety testing without running afoul of US President Donald

item.title: TSMC expected to report sixth straight quarter of record profit thanks to AI boom
item.description: Analysts say demand for Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co's (TSMC) AI chipmaking capacity, as well as its advanced chip packaging technology, CoWoS, remains strong.

item.title: The ET Startup Awards 2026 special
item.description: Happy Monday! The Economic Times Startup Awards (ETSA) 2026 ceremony brought together the country’s top founders, investors, and policymakers in Bengaluru for a Friday evening of sharp insights and spirited conversations.

item.title: ETSA champions show the great Indian dream is all home-brewed and visa-free: Union Minister Piyush Goyal
item.description: In a candid conversation with ET’s Deepshikha Sikarwar, he spoke about India’s trade deals, India-US relations, foreign investment, and how Indian businesses will benefit from the restrictions on the green card programme.

item.title: ETSA 2026: A secret circle, cosmic sparks and the night tech elite got goosebumps
item.description: The Closed-door Manifesto The unscripted room where minister Goyal’s call to arms met Bengaluru’s spirit, inspiring a tech elite primed for global dominance.

item.title: ET Startup Awards 2026 | Govt backing and patient capital propel India's leap into AI and chips: Satyan Gajwani
item.description: Gajwani said the ecosystem, once driven by fintech, food delivery, SaaS, commerce, quick commerce and direct-to-consumer brands, was witnessing founders focused on deep, proprietary technology. Indian startups are now building semiconductor chips, AI, robotics, clean energy technologies and new materials, while investors are shaping funds, willing to wait longer for these companies to mature.

item.title: ET Startup Awards 2026: Silicon Valley called. They want their wardrobe back!
item.description: The ET Startup Awards’ Silicon Valley dress code brought out puffer vests and sneakers, dresses where blazers might once have been, and silk saris worn with fitness watches. Striking a balance between boardroom polish and founder-casual ease, guests rounded off their looks with smart rings and trackers, turning the evening’s uniform into something more personal and data-driven.

item.title: ET Startup Awards 2026 | Tier-II cities rechart startup geography: IDFC First Bank’s Vaidyanathan
item.description: The startup story is not confined to a handful of sectors or cities, but is being shaped by talent and ideas across the country, Vaidyanathan said. About 52% of the startups banking with IDFC First Bank come from tier-II and -III locations, reflecting the widening geography of entrepreneurship, he said.

item.title: ETSA 2026: Over a decade on, India's startup story is only getting started
item.description: The 12th edition of The Economic Times Startup Awards (ETSA) captured this transition, reflecting an ecosystem that has moved beyond the race for scale to pursue technological depth, durable businesses and international markets.

item.title: Former Flipkart group employees launch petition seeking inclusion in proposed $2 billion Esop buyback
item.description: On October 10, a group of former executives launched a petition aiming to bring together 20,000-30,000 former employees of Flipkart and its group companies, including Myntra, Cleartrip, Shopsy, Super Money and ANS Commerce. The petition calls for their inclusion in the planned $2 billion Esop buyback.

item.title: Sequoia-backed chip startup Nuvacore raising funds at about a $2.5 billion valuation
item.description: Nuvacore is seeking to raise the funds as the appetite for central processors has swollen due to the thirst for data-crunching capacity to power chatbots such as Anthropic's Claude. CPUs perform vital functions as traffic controllers for Nvidia's AI chips and run autonomous AI software known as agents.

item.title: Qualcomm and Arm jury to return next week after deliberations in contract dispute case
item.description: The five-day trial that wrapped up this week was the second in two years between the companies, highlighting the deterioration of their business relationship after SoftBank Group acquired control of Arm in 2016 and Arm shifted from licensing the technology needed to make chips to selling chips of its own.

item.title: UPI MDR framework needs rationalisation to protect public trust: Report
item.description: UPI, a public digital infrastructure, has generated significant convenience for users and productivity gains for the economy, with its long-term economic benefits outweighing the incremental income that could accrue from merchant transaction fees, the report titled 'UPI at a Crossroads: Reintroducing the MDR' released by IIT Bombay said.

item.title: India's quick commerce growth set to accelerate, food delivery to remain steady: Report
item.description: According to the report, India's quick commerce sector is witnessing consolidation, with net order value (NOV) growth for leading platforms expected to accelerate to as much as 21.6% quarter-on-quarter in Q2FY27, as higher minimum order values and reduced discounts at some platforms shift demand towards competitors.

item.title: Ecommerce firms sell goods worth Rs 24,000 crore in first two days of festive sales: Redseer
item.description: Players like Amazon and Flipkart are using their quick commerce arms for sales and increasing their salience on the platform, which saw 4 to 5 times higher GMV than the BAU daily average.

item.title: India's tech push: five things to know
item.description: India has committed billions of dollars in semiconductors, electronics manufacturing and artificial intelligence in a bid to become a global technology powerhouse. India's electronics production rose from about $31 billion in 2014-15 to $133 billion in 2024-25, according to the government, which wants the country to become a tech manufacturing hub.

item.title: Google faces backlash against India data centre
item.description: Handcuffs encircle Google's logo on one campaign poster, while another warns that people "cannot drink data", as opposition mounts to the tech giant's planned AI mega-facility in India. Still, water use worries residents, especially given plans for Vizag to become a tech megahub.

item.title: Super Micro contractor pleads guilty in scheme to divert AI servers with Nvidia chips to China
item.description: In March, US prosecutors charged Ting-Wei "Willy" Sun and two others associated with Super Micro, including a co-founder, with conspiring to divert about $2.5 billion worth of US AI technology to China in violation of export laws.

item.title: Kalshi probes suspicious trades tied to Trump press secretary pick: WSJ
item.description: At least three small wagers were placed before news of Zacharia's selection emerged, potentially netting traders thousands of dollars in profits, the Journal reported.

item.title: Tessolve raises $75 million from US-based Vector Line Capital
item.description: Vector Line, a strategic investment company that invests exclusively in semiconductors and the chip supply chain, joins existing investors TPG and Novo Tellus. This is Vector Line's first investment in India, Tessolve said in a statement. The funds will support Tessolve's growth, including strategic acquisitions that add to its existing capabilities, widen its service offerings, and strengthen its global footprint.

item.title: Most trustworthy AI system demands least inherent model trust: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella
item.description: The most trustworthy Super Intelligence system will not be the one powered by the model users trust the most, but rather the system that allows people to trust the model the least, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella stated in a post on X.

item.title: Nvidia in talks to invest further in Reflection AI or buy it: FT
item.description: Talks are at an early stage and a deal could take several forms, including a so-called acqui-hire arrangement where Nvidia would hire staff and license technology rather than pursue a full acquisition, potentially avoiding a lengthy regulatory review, the newspaper said.

item.title: India's Infosys does not expect material impact from US PERM suspension
item.description: The US government said on Thursday it was suspending some major global tech and IT firms, including Infosys, from the PERM green card program, which allows skilled foreign workers to gain permanent residency in the US through their employment.

item.title: India Mobile Congress 2026 concludes with focus on agricultural AI, 5G automation and last-mile connectivity
item.description: Held over four days under the theme 'Scale Without Boundaries', the event brought together policymakers, industry leaders and technology developers to discuss applications of emerging technologies and their role in driving inclusive digital growth.

The ET Startup Awards 2026 special
item.description: Entrepreneurs, investors and policymakers came together in a star-studded event to honour the best of Indian entrepreneurship at the ET Startup Awards 2026 in Bengaluru.

item.title: ETSA 2026: Meesho, Groww CEOs on how life changes after an IPO
item.description: Aatrey said the company must continue to innovate while meeting the expectations of public-market investors. The need to set quarterly goals has also raised expectations within teams, making it important to balance predictability with innovation, he added.

item.title: If a startup can reach orbit, India can build AI the world wants: Satyan Gajwani, Chairman, Times Internet
ETSA 2026: Indian founders eyeing early IPOs instead of private capital: Meesho CEO Vidit Aatrey
item.description: Speaking at a panel alongside Groww CEO Lalit Keshre and ETtech editor Samidha Sharma, Aatrey contrasted India’s market with that of the United States.

item.title: Where will India's deep tech be in 10 years? Pixxel, Agrani Labs, BrainSight AI founders explain
Apple names insider Steve Smith as new M&A chief, memo shows
item.description: Perica, a more than 17-year veteran of Apple's M&A and corporate development function, also took oversight of iCloud, Fitness+ and News, among other businesses, in 2023, the memo written by services chief Eddy Cue said.

item.title: US announces effort to disrupt hacking infrastructure run by China's Integrity Tech Group
item.description: US officials say they are seizing seven internet domains in a new effort to disrupt hackers working with Chinese IT firm Integrity Technology Group.

item.title: SoftBank seeks $100 billion from Gulf states for AI
item.description: SoftBank Group Corp. is in discussions to raise up to $100 billion from Gulf investors for future AI investments. Founder Masayoshi Son has initiated talks with potential investors in the United Arab Emirates and surrounding regions. This proposed fund aims to enhance operations using AI technologies and robots from SoftBank's robotics arm Roze. SoftBank's shares fell recently due to concerns over OpenAI's revenue growth, prompting a reevaluation of investment strategies.

item.title: South Korea, Japan buffeted by hacks as AI lowers bar for cybercriminals
item.description: Nine South Korean banks and two mega-churches are probing cyberattacks that may have involved AI tools, while Japanese companies including Daiwa Securities, SoftBank Corp and the Lawson convenience store chain have been hit by a recent surge in cyber incidents.

item.title: Chinese developer makes ARTEX AI agent closed-source after Korean bank hack
item.description: The Chinese developer of ARTEX said they have converted the AI agent to a closed-source project after cybersecurity firms identified it as a tool used in a recent cyberattack campaign against South Korean banks.
